about: Offline API pre-sign guard and fast-market stop-loss docs contracts (BE-3904, BE-4292, BE-4343, BE-4344) recorded from the published release commit 5d7a861a8 (CLI 0.13.47, MCP 0.10.45, SDK 0.6.39): Jupiter 6001 slippage_exceeded classification, inner-CPI exclusion, redaction, maxSlippageBps default (100) and cap (5,000), countRisk: false, and Fast markets and stop losses docs parity plus offline fastConnectFetch execution. The SDK, MCP and CLI package contracts live in candle-presign-refused-packages.json.

error.message: The built transaction failed the pre-sign safety check (simulation_failed); nothing was signed or sent.
error.detail: The price moved past maxSlippageBps before the transaction could land; retry at once for a fresh quote, or raise maxSlippageBps (default 100, cap 5000). ({"InstructionError":[3,{"Custom":6001}]}; payer <payer> pool [redacted address]; Program [redacted address] failed: custom program error: 0x1771)

outcome.sdkDocsErrors: Every structured error response becomes a `CandleApiError` carrying `code`, `status`, `retryable`, and `field` where the API supplied one. A refused build (`reason: "presign_refused"`) also carries `refusal` (the pre-sign check that fired) and `detail` (its sentence for why, for example that the price moved past `maxSlippageBps`) from 0.6.37; nothing was signed or sent, so it is safe to build again. Branch on `code`, never on message text. Responses that are not structured envelopes throw the same error type with `code` set to `HTTP_<status>`.
outcome.sdkChangelogEntry: Release 0.6.37 (BE-4292); it carries the 0.6.36 code, so it waits on the same 2026-11-24T09:00Z gate. `CandleApiError` and `CandleErrorPayload` now carry `refusal` (the pre-sign check that fired) and `detail` (the server's redacted sentence for why) when the API sends them, as on a `presign_refused` build. A Jupiter slippage refusal's detail says the price moved past `maxSlippageBps`. No new method or request; an older API answers without them.
